description: Composite six-panel figure combining cross-sectional SEM micrographs and EBSD grain-boundary maps for three Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr low-density steels: (a, d) S1000, (b, e) S1050, (c, f) MHT per the caption. (a)–(c) are SEM images each with a 20 µm scale bar, white arrows labelled "twins", and scattered dark rounded pores; (a) additionally labels elongated strip-like precipitates lying along austenite grain boundaries as "Cr7C3" with a white arrow and circle, whereas (b) and (c) show no such grain-boundary precipitates. (d)–(f) are EBSD grain-boundary maps, each with legend boxes reading "Σ≤29" (red = special boundaries) and "RHABs" (thick black = random high-angle boundaries); the scale bars read 10 µm in (d) and (e) and 20 µm in (f). Each map carries an inset histogram of "Number Fraction" (y, 0–0.7) versus "Misorientation Angle/°" (x, 0–60), dominated by one tall bar at ~60° with minor bars near 35–50°. The 60° bar exceeds the 0.6 y-gridline in (d) and (f) and lies between 0.5 and 0.6 in (e). The figure demonstrates austenitic matrices with annealing twins in all three steels, Cr7C3 at grain boundaries only in S1000, and a Σ3-twin-dominated special-boundary population.

subfigures.description: Cross-sectional SEM micrograph of S1000 with a 20 µm scale bar; equiaxed austenite grains with dark rounded pores, white arrows labelled "twins", and elongated strip-like precipitates along grain boundaries pointed to by an arrow and circle labelled "Cr7C3".
Cross-sectional SEM micrograph of S1050 with a 20 µm scale bar; twins indicated by white arrows labelled "twins"; no grain-boundary precipitates labelled.
Cross-sectional SEM micrograph of MHT with a 20 µm scale bar; two white arrows labelled "twins"; matrix appears free of the elongated grain-boundary precipitates seen in (a).

EBSD grain-boundary map for S1000, 10 µm scale bar, with legend boxes "Σ≤29" (red) and "RHABs" (thick black lines); inset histogram of Number Fraction vs Misorientation Angle/° (0–60°) showing a dominant bar at ~60° above the 0.6 gridline.
EBSD grain-boundary map for S1050, 10 µm scale bar, same "Σ≤29"/"RHABs" legend; inset misorientation histogram with the 60° bar between the 0.5 and 0.6 gridlines and small bars near 38–40°.
EBSD grain-boundary map for MHT, 20 µm scale bar, same "Σ≤29"/"RHABs" legend; inset histogram whose 60° bar exceeds the 0.6 gridline; map shows many closely spaced red twin boundaries.

observations.observation: Panel (a) contains an explicit text label "Cr7C3" with a white arrow/circle pointing at elongated strip-like precipitates decorating austenite grain boundaries in S1000.
Panels (b) and (c) carry only "twins" labels and show no elongated grain-boundary precipitates comparable to those labelled in (a).

The EBSD maps (d)–(f) carry legend boxes reading "Σ≤29" in red and "RHABs" in grey, indicating that red lines mark special boundaries and thick black lines mark random high-angle boundaries, as the caption/citing text confirms.

The inset histograms in (d)–(f) are plotted as Number Fraction (y-axis, 0 to 0.7) versus Misorientation Angle/° (x-axis, 0 to 60), with a single dominant bar at ~60° and only small bars in the 30–50° range.
The histogram bar at 60° rises above the 0.6 gridline in (d) and (f) and lies between the 0.5 and 0.6 gridlines in (e); this is read from gridlines, not from printed data labels.
Scale bars are printed as 20 µm in (a), (b) and (c), 10 µm in (d) and (e), and 20 µm in (f).
The caption labels the panels as cross-sectional SEM and misorientation angle distribution micrographs of (a, d) S1000, (b, e) S1050 and (c, f) MHT.
The citing text states that the matrix microstructures of all steels comprise austenite and that the strip-like precipitates in S1000 are identified as Cr7C3 by TEM.
The citing text states effective grain sizes d_eff of 3.17, 3.84 and 7.31 µm for S1000, S1050 and MHT respectively; no such values are printed in the figure.
The citing text states that most annealing twins have a Σ3 orientation relationship with the parent grains, consistent with the ~60° peak in panels (d)–(f).
The citing text reports special-boundary (Σ ≤ 29) proportions of 71.7 %, 68.3 % and 71.2 % for S1000, S1050 and MHT, with S1050 lowest; these percentages are not printed on the figure.

The citing text states that the number of twins increases in MHT but their size becomes smaller, i.e. more nucleation sites with suppressed growth; the maps in (f) do show numerous closely spaced red twin boundaries.

unreadable_items: histogram inset in (d): the exact height of the small bars near 35–50° is not resolvable beyond 'low number fraction'
individual pixel-level index colors in the grey EBSD maps (d–f) are not distinguishable; only the red special-boundary and black RHAB lines are legible
no numeric value is printed for the 60° peak so its height is only estimated relative to the printed y gridlines
